essay_tasks.task: Discuss the importance of maintaining a balanced nature and explain the roles humans play in ensuring the sustainability of living things. [10 marks]

critique.real_spm_equivalent: This imitates an SPM Bahasa Inggeris 1119 Paper 1 Section A Directed Writing task (35 marks: format 3 + content 12 + language 20, ~45 min, 200-250 words) or a Sejarah 1249 Kertas 2 Bahagian A structured item (40 marks for 4 items, so ~10 marks each). It does NOT match Continuous Writing (50 marks, 1 of 5 titles, no guiding stimulus).
critique.teacher_verdict: The wording 'Discuss the importance of ... and explain the roles ...' with a stimulus block is not how 1119 Directed Writing is phrased — real questions name the text type (speech, article, report, letter) and give a purpose/audience, and Continuous Writing gives no stimulus. A 10-mark cap with a 3-band holistic rubric is neither the 35-mark 1119 scheme (format/content/language) nor the Sejarah point-based Peraturan Pemarkahan; the model answer is ~200 words, far short of a 200-250 word Directed Writing and nowhere near a 350+ word essay.
critique.student_view: This doesn't look like any real 1119 question I've practised — there's no text type, no audience, and 10 marks with an A/B/C band feels like a school worksheet, not SPM. The model answer is fine English but it's just two body paragraphs of generalities; it wouldn't show me how to hit the format marks or the content points an examiner actually ticks.
fixes: Rewrite the stem as a real 1119 Directed Writing task: name the text type and audience, e.g. 'Write a speech to be delivered to your school's Environment Club on the importance of maintaining a balanced nature and the roles humans play in sustainability', and set it at 35 marks with the format/content/language split.
If the intent is Sejarah Kertas 2 Bahagian A, restate as a structured item with (a)/(b)/(c) sub-parts and mark each by isi/huraian points (e.g. 4+3+3), not a holistic A/B/C band.

Replace the 3-band holistic rubric with the actual 1119 Directed Writing scheme (format 3, content 12, language 20) or a point-based mark scheme listing acceptable content points and 1 mark per valid isi/huraian.

Lengthen the model answer to the required 200-250 words for Directed Writing (or 350+ for Continuous Writing) and make it demonstrate the named format features (salutation, opening, closing) so it models the marks being awarded.

critique.teacher_verdict: This is not an SPM 1119 task: Continuous Writing is 50 marks with a choice of five titles and no stimulus, and Directed Writing is 35 marks with a specified text type and format marks. A 10-mark stimulus essay with a three-band holistic rubric has no counterpart in the real paper, and the model answer is far too short for any 1119 composition. The theme is suitable for teenagers, but the task teaches none of the skills the real paper rewards.
critique.student_view: I have never seen a 10-mark essay with a stimulus in 1119 — Section B gives me five titles and 50 marks, and Section A makes me write a letter or speech with format marks. The model answer is only about 200 words, so it would not even meet the length requirement of a real composition, and the rubric bands do not match the 1119 language bands I have been trained on.
fixes: Replace the task with a genuine 1119 Section B Continuous Writing prompt: one of five titles (e.g. 'Friendship' discursive/reflective), 50 marks, ~350-500 words, no stimulus and no bullet points.
If a stimulus-based task is intended, relabel it as a school-based assessment or textbook exercise, not SPM 1119, and remove the 'SPM' framing.

Rewrite the rubric to match the 1119 Continuous Writing bands (A 44-50, B 38-43, etc.) with descriptors on accuracy, sentence variety, vocabulary, paragraphing, relevance and reader interest, not a three-band 1-10 scale.

Expand the model answer to at least 350 words with a clear introduction, developed body paragraphs on each friendship level and on mutual effort/boundaries, and a conclusion, so it models the length and structure the real paper demands.

essay_tasks.label: cached: Bahasa Inggeris
essay_tasks.task: Based on the patterns of friendship, explain the four levels of friendship keakraban (intimacy) and discuss how the level of communication influences the strength of these relationships. [10 marks]

critique.real_spm_equivalent: This does not match any real SPM Bahasa Inggeris 1119 task. It most resembles a Sejarah 1249 Kertas 2 Bahagian B structured/essay item (answer 3 of 7, 60 marks, points-based marking) or a Bahasa Melayu 1103 Kertas 2 Pemahaman/KOMSAS item, but it is written in English with a social-psychology textbook frame. Real 1119 Paper 1 Section B Continuous Writing is 50 marks, choose 1 of 5 titles, about 1 hour, no stimulus and no bullet points; Section A Directed Writing is 35 marks with a text type and stimulus. A 10-mark 'explain four levels and discuss' item has no home in 1119.
critique.teacher_verdict: This is not an SPM Bahasa Inggeris composition task at all: 1119 never sets a 10-mark 'explain four levels and discuss' item with a stimulus paragraph, and the mixed Malay/English terminology (keakraban, kenalan, sahabat intim) belongs to a BM or Sejarah paper, not 1119. The rubric is a generic holistic band scheme, whereas SPM 1119 marks content and language separately (Directed Writing: format 3 + content 12 + language 20) and Sejarah marks by isi/huraian points. As a classroom exercise it is usable, but it would mislead a candidate about what the real paper demands.
critique.student_view: If I saw this in an exam I would assume I had opened the wrong paper — 1119 gives me five essay titles and 50 marks, not a 10-mark textbook recall with a stimulus about Adam. The model answer is fine English but it just lists the textbook's four levels; there is no format, no directed-writing text type, and the rubric tells me nothing about how content and language marks are actually split.
fixes: Replace with a genuine 1119 Paper 1 Section B task: one of five titles, 50 marks, about 1 hour, e.g. 'Write a story about a friendship that changed you' or a discursive title on friendship, with no stimulus paragraph and no bullet points.

If the intention is Directed Writing, recast as Section A: 35 marks (format 3 + content 12 + language 20), specify the text type (e.g. an article for the school magazine) and give the stimulus as notes/points to develop, not as a mini-textbook.

Remove the Malay terms (keakraban, kenalan, sahabat biasa, sahabat karib, sahabat intim) or move the whole item to Bahasa Melayu 1103 Kertas 2, where such vocabulary and a 10-mark item would be plausible.

Replace the A/B/C holistic rubric with the real 1119 marking dimensions (content points + language band descriptors for accuracy, sentence variety, vocabulary, paragraphing, relevance) so the feedback teaches how marks are actually awarded.

essay_tasks.label: cached: Sejarah
essay_tasks.task: Discuss the importance of empire formation to the Malacca Sultanate from political and economic perspectives, and explain how the administration of these territories was structured. [10 marks]

critique.real_spm_equivalent: Sejarah 1249/2 Bahagian B (essay), where candidates answer 3 of 7 questions at 20 marks each (60 marks total). A 10-mark sub-question with a stimulus paragraph does not match the real essay section; it more closely resembles a Bahagian A structured item, but those are 10 marks each within a 40-mark section and are not framed as a free essay with a Band A/B/C language rubric.
critique.teacher_verdict: The content is on-syllabus and the model answer is a reasonable Band-6-style response, but the task framing is wrong for SPM Sejarah: a 10-mark stimulus essay with a language-band rubric does not exist in 1249/2. Real Sejarah marking is point-based (isi/huraian) per Peraturan Pemarkahan, not holistic A/B/C bands, so the rubric would actively mislead a candidate about how marks are earned.
critique.student_view: If I write this in the real paper I get marked by isi and huraian points, not by 'fluent language with minimal errors' — so this rubric teaches me the wrong thing. Also, 10 marks for a full essay with intro, body and conclusion feels too cheap; real Bahagian B essays are 20 marks each.
fixes: Re-cast as a Sejarah 1249/2 Bahagian B essay at 20 marks (answer 3 of 7), or as a Bahagian A structured item with (a)/(b)/(c) sub-parts totalling 10 marks — not a single free essay.

Replace the A/B/C language-band rubric with a point-based Peraturan Pemarkahan: list expected isi points (e.g. political: blocking Siam/Majapahit, regional stability; economic: tribute, Straits control, spice/agri supply) each with huraian marks, and state 'any X points'.
Remove the language-fluency descriptors entirely — Sejarah is not marked on grammar or style; keep only content accuracy and explanation depth.

Tighten the stimulus to a short factual stem (dates, key terms) as in real papers, and drop the 'Discuss... from political and economic perspectives' phrasing in favour of SPM command words like 'Nyatakan' / 'Jelaskan' / 'Huraikan' with explicit mark splits.

Expand the model answer to at least 350 patah perkataan with an introduction, 4-5 developed isi, and a conclusion, and add at least one peribahasa/ungkapan menarik to model Band 6 language.
Remove the 'Berdasarkan maklumat berikut' prose stimulus if this is meant to be a BM karangan — real BM Kertas 1 Bahagian B gives only a 1-2 sentence prompt and one instruction word.

essay_tasks.label: BM karangan
essay_tasks.task: Penggunaan telefon pintar dalam kalangan murid sekolah kini semakin meluas dan sukar dibendung. Ada pihak berpendapat bahawa telefon pintar banyak mendatangkan kebaikan kepada murid, manakala ada pula yang berpandangan sebaliknya. Bincangkan pernyataan tersebut. Panjang karangan anda hendaklah lebih daripada 350 patah perkataan.

critique.real_spm_equivalent: BM 1103 Kertas 1 Bahagian B (karangan respons terbuka), real allocation 100 markah, >350 patah perkataan, ~1h30m, choose 1 of 5 questions
critique.teacher_verdict: The question stem is genuinely SPM-shaped: a two-sided stimulus plus 'Bincangkan' and the >350-word instruction, exactly the Bahagian B genre. But the 70-mark cap is wrong — Bahagian B is 100 markah — and the three-band rubric (62-70 / 38-61 / 1-37) is a coarse invention, not the Lembaga Peperiksaan holistic band scheme with its language criteria (gramatis, kosa kata, unsur bahasa bervariasi, ungkapan menarik, ejaan). The model answer opens well but at ~2300 characters it is nowhere near 350 words, so it does not itself satisfy the length it demands.
critique.student_view: The question reads like a real 'Bincangkan' soalan, but 70 marks and three bands tell me nothing about how I'd actually be graded — real marking is holistic against language criteria, not a 62-70 window. And the sample answer stops mid-sentence at 'Lebih membimban...' and is clearly under 350 words, so I can't use it as a length model.
fixes: Change MAX MARKS to 100 (Bahagian B real allocation) and state the ~1h30m suggested time.
Replace the three-band rubric with the real holistic criteria: isi, pengolahan, and bahasa (gramatis, kosa kata luas dan tepat, unsur bahasa bervariasi, ungkapan menarik, ejaan rumi betul).
Complete the model answer and expand it to at least 350 patah perkataan (currently ~2300 chars, well short) so it models the required length.
Keep the two-sided stimulus but ensure the model answer gives a clear pendirian/kesimpulan, since 'Bincangkan' scripts are marked on balanced argument plus a stance.

essay_tasks.label: English directed writing
essay_tasks.task:
Write an article for your school magazine on the topic 'Social Media and Teenagers'. In your article, you must:

• describe the benefits of social media for teenagers
• discuss the negative effects of social media on teenagers
• suggest ways teenagers can use social media responsibly

Write your article in about 150–200 words.

critique.real_spm_equivalent: SPM Bahasa Inggeris 1119 Paper 1 Section A (Directed Writing), 35 marks, ~45 minutes, 150-200 words — this matches the real format closely.
critique.teacher_verdict: The task is a solid imitation of SPM 1119 Directed Writing: correct text type, 35 marks, 150-200 words, and a stimulus notice that is plausible. However, the real paper does not usually give three bullet points in the question; it gives a short stimulus and one instruction, with content points implied by the stimulus. The rubric is too generic and lacks the real 3+12+20 split (format, content, language), so it would not train students to score marks accurately.
critique.student_view: This looks like a real directed writing question, but the three bullets feel like a checklist that the real SPM paper would not hand me — I'd expect to infer content from the stimulus. The model answer is good but a bit too neat and short; I'd want to see how to develop each point with specific examples to hit Band A.
fixes: Remove the three bullet points and instead embed the required content points in the stimulus notice (e.g., 'discuss both benefits and drawbacks, and include practical advice') to match the real SPM format where content points are not listed as bullets.

Replace the generic A-D rubric with the actual SPM 1119 Section A marking scheme: Format 3 marks, Content 12 marks, Language 20 marks, with band descriptors for language (Band A 16-20, etc.) and explicit content point allocation.

Expand the model answer to 180-200 words and add more specific, developed examples (e.g., name a platform, give a statistic or personal anecdote) to demonstrate Band A content development and varied sentence structures.

Add a note on time allocation (about 45 minutes) and word count guidance (150-200 words) as in the real paper, and ensure the stimulus notice is dated and signed like a real school notice to increase authenticity.

(c) Should Students Be Allowed to Use Mobile Phones in School? (discursive/argumentative)
(d) The Person Who Taught Me the Meaning of Hard Work (reflective)

[At least 250 words]

critique.real_spm_equivalent: English 1119 Paper 1 Section B Continuous Writing: choose 1 of 5 titles, 50 marks, about 1 hour, no stimulus/guiding points. Real papers typically specify 'not less than 350 words' (some older schemes say about 350); the 250-word minimum here is below the usual SPM standard.
critique.teacher_verdict: The 50-mark continuous writing format and four genre-labelled titles are close to the real 1119 Section B, but the 'at least 250 words' instruction is noticeably below the SPM norm (usually 350) and the genre labels in brackets are more helpful than a real paper. The model answer is competent Band A/B prose but is only about 400 words, so it does not demonstrate the sustained development expected at the top band.
critique.student_view: This looks like a simplified version of Section B — the titles are fine, but real papers say 350 words and do not label each title with its genre. The model answer reads well but feels short for a 50-mark essay, so I would not trust it as a full-mark exemplar.
fixes: Change the length instruction to 'Write a composition of not less than 350 words' to match the real 1119 Section B requirement.
Remove the genre labels in brackets (narrative/descriptive/discursive/reflective) so the task mirrors the real paper's bare titles.
Extend the model answer to at least 500–600 words with fuller paragraph development to model Band A sustained relevance and reader interest.
Add a note that the 50 marks are awarded holistically by band (A 44–50 etc.) rather than by point-counting, to match the real marking approach.

essay_tasks.label: 华文 作文
essay_tasks.task:
题目：手机对青少年是利大于弊还是弊大于利？
文体：议论文
写作提示：
• 表明你的立场，并说明理由。
• 举出生活中的例子或数据来支持你的论点。
• 针对反方观点进行反驳，并提出建议。
（字数不少于500个汉字）

critique.real_spm_equivalent: Bahasa Cina (华文) SPM Kertas 1 (writing), Bahagian B 作文 — the long essay, 70 marks, 1h45m total for the whole paper (Bahagian A 30 + Bahagian B 70). Real Bahagian B typically offers a choice of several titles (e.g. 议论文/记叙文/说明文 options) and a minimum word count around 500 字; the exact current Lembaga Peperiksaan wording and whether 3 bullet hints appear is not something I can verify with high confidence.
critique.teacher_verdict: The topic, genre label (议论文) and 70-mark allocation are plausible for SPM 华文 Bahagian B, but the three bullet '写作提示' are not how the real paper presents a 作文 — real questions give a title and a word count, not a scaffolded argument plan. The model answer is far too short (650 字 vs the stated 不少于500, and real top scripts run longer) and is a formulaic four-paragraph essay that would sit in 良好, not 优秀.
critique.student_view: The bullets basically tell me the whole essay structure — real SPM never does that, so this feels like a textbook exercise, not a paper. And the 'model answer' is only 650 characters when it asks for 500+; it reads like a safe Band-2 script, not something that would get 62-70.
fixes: Remove the three 写作提示 bullets; present it as a real 作文 question: just the title/statement plus 字数不少于500个汉字, and ideally offer a choice of 2-3 titles as the real Bahagian B does.
Make the model answer actually meet and exceed the word count — aim for 700-900 汉字 with a fuller 引论-本论(2-3段)-结论 structure, at least two concrete examples/data points, and a genuine 反驳 paragraph.
Strengthen the model answer's language to 优秀 standard: varied sentence patterns, 成语/修辞, precise 标点, and avoid the clichéd '刀能切菜也能伤人' analogy which is overused and weak.
Align the rubric to the real 华文 marking dimensions (内容/表达/结构/文体 with 错别字 and 字数 penalties) rather than three generic bands; the current 及格 band starting at 1 mark is unrealistic.

essay_tasks.label: Sejarah content essay
essay_tasks.task: Huraikan faktor-faktor yang mencetuskan kebangkitan nasionalisme di Tanah Melayu. [10 markah]

critique.real_spm_equivalent: Sejarah 1249 Kertas 2, Bahagian B (esai berstruktur), soalan 'Huraikan faktor...' — real Bahagian B essays are 20 marks each (answer 3 of 7, 60 marks total), not 10 marks; a 10-mark 'Huraikan' item resembles a Bahagian A structured sub-question (40 marks, 4 questions, ~10 marks per question with several sub-parts), not a standalone essay.
critique.teacher_verdict: The topic is SPM-appropriate Sejarah content, but the packaging is wrong: a 10-mark 'Huraikan' essay with a stimulus paragraph and a generic Band A/B/C language rubric does not match Sejarah Kertas 2, which marks by isi/huraian points per Peraturan Pemarkahan (Bahagian B essays are 20 marks; Bahagian A structured items are ~10 marks but split into sub-parts). The model answer is a decent BM essay but reads like a Bahasa Melayu karangan, not a Sejarah script — it lacks the point-per-mark density and specific evidence an examiner rewards.
critique.student_view: This looks like a BM karangan pasted onto a Sejarah question — real Sejarah Kertas 2 gives me 20 marks for an essay and marks me on isi and huraian, not on 'bahasa lancar'. Also, if it's 10 marks, where are the sub-parts (a)(b)(c) I'd normally see in Bahagian A?
fixes: Change to a real Sejarah Kertas 2 Bahagian B essay: 'Huraikan faktor-faktor yang mencetuskan kebangkitan nasionalisme di Tanah Melayu. [20 markah]' — or keep 10 marks but restructure as a Bahagian A item with sub-parts, e.g. (a) pengaruh luar [4m], (b) media massa [3m], (c) pendidikan [3m].
Remove the stimulus paragraph if it is a Bahagian B essay (real Bahagian B essays are a single instruction, no bullet/paragraph hints), or keep it only if mimicking a Bahagian A stimulus-based item.

Replace the generic Band A/B/C language rubric with a Sejarah point-based scheme: list isi (1 mark) + huraian (1 mark) per factor, with 'any X points' and explicit fakta accepted (e.g. Revolusi China 1911, Gerakan Islah, Al-Imam, Utusan Melayu, sekolah vernakular/agama).

Rewrite the model answer as a Sejarah script: lead with a short definition, then 3 factors each with 2–3 specific facts + elaboration to hit the point count, and drop the BM-karangan framing ('Bahasa lancar', 'kesimpulan' flourish) that does not earn Sejarah marks.

essay_tasks.label: Biology content essay
essay_tasks.task: Discuss how human activities can disrupt the balance of an ecosystem and explain the measures that can be taken to maintain a balanced ecosystem. [10 marks]

critique.real_spm_equivalent: This imitates SPM Biology 4551 Paper 2 Bahagian B (structured/essay section), where a 10-mark essay question on ecosystem balance would be answered in about 8-12 minutes within a 2h30m paper; it also loosely resembles a SPM English 1119 Section B discursive essay, but that is 50 marks and ~350+ words, not 10 marks.
critique.teacher_verdict: The task wording and 10-mark allocation are plausible for a Biology Paper 2 essay, but the stimulus is a textbook paragraph rather than the data/graph/table SPM usually provides, and the rubric is a generic language-band scheme, not the point-based isi/huraian marking used in Biology. The model answer is accurate but reads like a summary, not a top-band script with elaborated mechanisms and specific examples.
critique.student_view: This feels like a comprehension summary, not an SPM Biology essay — where's the stimulus figure and the mark-per-point breakdown? The model answer just lists causes and measures without explaining how each works, so I can't see how to earn the 10 marks.
fixes: Replace the text stimulus with an SPM-style stimulus: a graph or table showing deforestation rate vs. CO2 level, or a diagram of an ecosystem with human activities labelled.
Rewrite the rubric to match Biology point-based marking: e.g., 1 mark per correct cause + explanation, 1 mark per measure + explanation, max 10, with 'any five' style.

Expand the model answer to show elaborated mechanisms (e.g., how deforestation reduces carbon sinks and disrupts the carbon cycle) and include specific Malaysian examples (palm oil plantations, haze from forest fires).

Add a command-word instruction in Bahasa Melayu/English as in real SPM: 'Explain how human activities disrupt ecosystem balance and suggest measures to maintain it. [10 marks]' and specify answer length (e.g., 100-150 words).

rows.label: BM karangan
rows.feedback: Anda berjaya mengembangkan setiap isi dengan contoh konkrit seperti YouTube dan Google Classroom, dan bahasa anda gramatis serta mudah difahami. Namun, huraian anda tentang keburukan telefon pintar agak ringkas berbanding bahagian kebaikan, menyebabkan perbincangan tidak seimbang; sebagai contoh, anda hanya menyebut 'buli siber' tanpa menjelaskan kesannya secara mendalam. Cuba tambah satu atau dua ayat huraian lanjut bagi setiap keburukan yang dinyatakan, seperti mengaitkannya dengan kesan jangka panjang terhadap sahsiah murid.
improvements: Seimbangkan huraian antara kebaikan dan keburukan; berikan lebih banyak contoh dan kesan untuk bahagian keburukan.
Elakkan pengulangan frasa 'selain itu' yang terlalu kerap; gunakan penanda wacana lain seperti 'seterusnya', 'lebih-lebih lagi', 'di samping itu'.
Pastikan setiap perenggan mempunyai ayat topik yang jelas di awal perenggan sebelum huraian.
rows.model_structure:

rows.feedback: You clearly conveyed your father's quiet dedication through concrete details like his oil-stained hands and his decision to work despite a fever. However, your writing is weakened by frequent subject-verb agreement errors, such as 'he wake up' and 'he never miss', which disrupt the flow. For immediate improvement, proofread your next draft specifically for third-person singular verbs—add '-s' or '-es' where needed—and rewrite each incorrect sentence aloud to hear the correct form.
improvements: Subject-verb agreement: Ensure verbs match singular subjects (e.g., 'he wakes up', 'he never misses', 'he has small cuts').
Tense consistency: Use past tense consistently when narrating past events (e.g., 'he came home', 'he smiled').
Sentence variety: Add more complex sentences and avoid repetitive 'He will...' structures; use conjunctions and varied openings.
Vocabulary range: Replace basic words like 'very tired' with more precise alternatives (e.g., 'exhausted', 'weary').
Punctuation: Use apostrophes correctly for possessives (e.g., 'my father's workshop').

critique.teacher_verdict: The script is competent but not 'excellent': it is 380 words (over the 350 limit, which real SPM penalises), and the feedback ignores this and the imbalance it mentions. The mark of 58/70 is too high for a script with limited vocabulary, repetitive connectors, and no clear thesis; a real marker would place it in the 48-54 range. The feedback uses generic terms like 'gramatis' and 'mudah difahami' without citing specific language errors or isi gaps, and the improvement list is not tied to the actual script.
critique.student_view: This feedback tells me to balance my points and vary connectors, but it doesn't show me exactly which sentences are weak or how to fix them, so I can't see how to gain the next 10 marks. It also doesn't mention that I exceeded the word limit, which is a real SPM penalty.

critique.teacher_verdict: The script is a balanced two-sided discussion of a stimulus topic, but 48/70 (Baik) is generous for a 255-word essay with shallow huraian and no peribahasa; a trained marker would place it in the Sederhana/Memadai band, roughly 30-36/70. The feedback correctly identifies shallow huraian and cites the student's own words, but it never names the SPM dimensions (isi, bahasa, pengolahan) or the band criteria, and it does not tell the student the actual mark breakdown or how many marks each improvement is worth.
critique.student_view: The feedback tells me my huraian is too short and gives me a model opening, which is useful, but it does not tell me how the 70 marks are split between isi, bahasa and pengolahan, so I cannot see which part is costing me the most. It also does not warn me that 255 words is far below the 'lebih daripada 350 patah perkataan' requirement, which is the single biggest reason my mark would be capped in the real paper.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 237-word script that is mostly general statements with shallow, repetitive huraian and a thin conclusion would not sit at 38/70 under the BM 1103 holistic band criteria; a trained marker would place it lower, around the Sederhana band, because isi is present but huraian and bahasa do not carry it. The feedback correctly names the shallow-huraian weakness but never anchors the mark to the official dimensions (isi, bahasa, pengolahan) or explains the band, so the 38/70 figure looks inflated and unjustified.
critique.student_view: The advice to add a concrete example and its kesan is genuinely useful and I could act on it, but the 38/70 tells me nothing about which band I am in or how many marks each weakness is costing me. I would not know how to climb from here to the next band because the feedback never mentions isi/bahasa/pengolahan or the word-count and conclusion requirements that SPM actually marks.

critique.teacher_verdict: 30/35 sits in the top band for a script whose format is incomplete and whose content is asserted rather than developed; a real 1119 marker would deduct format marks first (title/byline/sign-off are part of the 3 format marks) and then judge content coverage and language, landing nearer 24-28. The feedback correctly spots the format gap but never quotes the script, never separates format/content/language marks, and never says how many marks each fix is worth.
critique.student_view: It tells me to add a title and byline, which is genuinely useful, but it doesn't tell me how many marks that is worth or whether my content and language are actually band A, so I can't tell what else to fix. The 'how it should look' outline is just a summary of my own essay, not a model of SPM-standard development.

critique.teacher_verdict: The 23/35 (Band B) is generous for a script the app itself admits is riddled with subject-verb and word-form errors; under the 1119 Directed Writing scheme (Format 3 + Content 12 + Language 20) a script with repeated basic accuracy errors and a thin, formulaic body would sit in the lower-mid language band, giving roughly 17-21. The feedback also never states the mark breakdown (format/content/language) or names the text-type conventions being judged, so it does not read like a real marker's report.
critique.student_view: It flags two real errors in my own words, which is useful, but it never tells me how the 35 marks are split or which band I'm in, so I can't see what specifically to fix to jump a band. The 'how it should look' outline is just a model answer, not a marking guide, so it won't reliably raise my SPM score.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 156-word script that is short of the ~250-word expectation, with simple repetitive sentences and an incomplete final sentence, cannot sit in Band C for 1119 Directed Writing where language carries 20 of the 35 marks. The feedback also invents content points ('all three content points') and quotes a sentence ('Some teenagers spend too much time...') that does not appear in the script shown, which is a serious credibility failure for a marker.
critique.student_view: The advice about developing points with examples is genuinely useful, but the mark of 19/35 is flattering and the feedback quotes sentences I never wrote, so I would not trust it to tell me where I actually stand. It never tells me the real gap: my script is too short and my language band is low, and that is what costs the marks in Section A.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 44/50 (Band A) is generous for a 428-word narrative that is competent but leans on stock imagery ('sun beat down mercilessly', 'heart hammering', 'reservoir of grit'); a trained 1119 marker would more likely place this in the upper Band B/low Band A boundary, around 38-42. The feedback never once references the actual SPM Continuous Writing band descriptors (accuracy, varied sentence structure, wide precise vocabulary, paragraph linkage, sustained reader interest) and instead invents a 'deepen the reflection' rubric that is not how Section B is marked.
critique.student_view: This tells me to rewrite my last paragraph and avoid clichés, but it doesn't tell me which band descriptor I'm losing marks on, so I can't target the next mark. In the real exam I'd want to know if my problem is vocabulary range, sentence variety, or relevance—not just 'add a concrete action'.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 32/50 (Band C) is generous for a script with repeated third-person singular errors, article slips and thin paragraphing; a trained 1119 marker would more likely place this in the 24-28 range (upper Band D / low Band C) on the Section B 50-mark scale. The feedback correctly identifies real errors, but it never frames the judgement in the actual 1119 Section B band descriptors (accuracy, varied sentence structure, wide precise vocabulary, well-planned linked paragraphs, sustained reader interest), so the student cannot see how the mark was derived.
critique.student_view: The error list is genuinely useful and quotes my own sentences, so I can fix the -s endings and articles. But it doesn't tell me what separates a 32 from a 40 in SPM terms — vocabulary range, paragraph linking, reader interest — so I'd fix grammar and still not know how to climb a band.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 30/50 (Band C) is generous for a 294-word script with pervasive tense slippage, simple repeated sentence patterns and thin content — a real 1119 marker working the 50-mark Continuous Writing bands would more likely land in the 20-24 range (Band D/E boundary), since accuracy and vocabulary range are the dominant criteria and both are weak here. The feedback correctly diagnoses tense as the biggest gap, but it never frames the judgement in the actual Section B band descriptors (accuracy, varied sentence structure, wide precise vocabulary, paragraph organisation, sustained reader interest) and never mentions that the script is short of a full-length response.
critique.student_view: The tense advice is genuinely useful and quotes my own sentences, so I could act on it — but it doesn't tell me how the 50 marks are actually split, so I don't know whether fixing tenses alone moves me from C to B or whether I also need length, vocabulary range and paragraph planning. It reads like generic English-teacher correction rather than an SPM marker telling me which band descriptor I failed.
